input.summary:
Customer reports their card was charged twice yesterday, and possibly earlier, despite not having launched any campaigns, and is requesting a refund for these charges.

Billing summary findings:
- Two Pro subscription charges recorded on 2026-09-07: ch_x43 ($252.00, succeeded) and ch_x44 ($185.00, succeeded), alongside four failed attempts of $185.00 each on the same date (ch_x37, ch_x38, ch_x39, ch_x40), all unrefunded.
- Two more charges recorded on 2026-10-07: ch_x41 ($144.00) and ch_x42 ($185.00), both succeeded, both marked not refunded.
- No refunds are recorded for this organization (recentRefunds is empty).
- The billing reconciliation check itself flagged: "Stripe shows a succeeded charge, but the product database has no active subscription status. Check whether this organization was charged without being provisioned." This is a system-generated flag, not a conclusion I've drawn independently.
- Two active Stripe subscriptions were found (sub_x49 and sub_x50), which may explain duplicate monthly/creation charges if the customer was signed up twice, but no result in what I can see ties a specific charge to confirmation of which subscription or order it paid for, or confirms whether the customer intended or authorized two subscriptions.
- Customer states they have not launched any campaigns, which is unverified here and relevant to whether the account was used to justify the charges.

Unresolved questions for billing to reconcile:
- Whether the two active Stripe subscriptions reflect an intentional duplicate signup or a billing-side error.
- Which specific charges the customer considers duplicate (exact dates/amounts from their statement) to match against the above.
- Whether any of the charges should be refunded given the reconciliation flag and lack of recorded refunds.

This needs human billing review rather than an automated verdict, since it involves reconciling possible duplicate subscriptions and a system-flagged charge/provisioning mismatch.
